transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi, thanks. Well, I came in because... things have just been a bit much lately. Ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, I've noticed I'm just a lot more wound up and short-tempered than I'm used to being. 

I mean, I'm holding it together at work alright, but at home and with my coursework, it's a different story. And I've started skipping out on the things that usually keep my head clear—fishing, my woodworking, even the first-aid workshops I usually go to. I just haven't been doing them. So, I figured I should probably come in and talk to someone about it.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like fishing, woodworking, or your first-aid workshops?

Well, no, I wouldn't say I've lost interest in them. I still want to do them... I mean, I still like the idea of going fishing or getting out into the woodshop. It's just that with everything going on at the house right now, I haven't really had the time or the energy to actually do any of it. But if I did go, I'm sure I'd still enjoy it.
Have you noticed feeling down, sad, or depressed most of the day, even when things aren’t particularly stressful?

No, I wouldn't say I feel depressed or sad most of the day. I mean, I get frustrated and stressed out when I'm at home, sure, because of the situation with my father-in-law. But when I'm at work or just going about my day, I feel pretty normal. It's really just the stress at the house that's getting to me, not a constant sadness or anything like that.
Have you found yourself feeling more irritable or easily angered lately, especially in response to the stress at home?

Yeah, like I mentioned earlier, I definitely am. It's mostly just... being short-tempered around the house. Like, I'll snap a little quicker than I normally would if things get chaotic or if my father-in-law is needing a lot of attention. 

I'm not, you know, flying into a rage or anything like that. Just... my patience is a lot thinner right now.
Have you noticed yourself being less motivated or less active in general, even when it comes to things that aren't related to the situation at home?

No, I wouldn't say that. When I'm at work, I'm just as active and focused as I've always been. You know, doing my job as an EMT, you kind of have to stay on your toes, and I haven't had any trouble with that at all. 

It's really just the situation at the house that drains my energy. Outside of that, my motivation is fine. I'm keeping up with everything else normally.
Have you noticed feeling unusually restless, on edge, or having trouble relaxing, especially since your father-in-law moved in?

Yeah, I guess you could say I'm more wound up. Like I said, I'm holding it together at work just fine, but at home... and even with my coursework... I'm definitely more on edge and short than I'm used to being. 

It's actually why I came in. I've even started skipping the things that usually help me relax and keep my head clear, like fishing, woodworking, and the first-aid workshops I usually go to. I just haven't been doing them since he moved in.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep lately, like needing less sleep or having trouble falling or staying asleep?

No, my sleep hasn't really changed. I'm still sleeping about the same as I always do. I don't have any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, and I definitely don't feel like I need less of it. Sleep's been fine.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things outside of the situation at home, like work, school, or other responsibilities, even when there's no immediate problem?

No, not really. I mean, work is stressful by nature, being an EMT, but I don't sit around worrying about it when I'm off the clock. And school... well, I'm a little frustrated with myself for getting behind on my coursework, but I wouldn't say I'm constantly worrying about it or anything else. It's really just the stuff at home with my father-in-law that's eating at me. Everything else is pretty much normal.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you're not good enough, especially in relation to the situation at home?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm definitely frustrated with how things are going at home, but I don't feel like it's my fault or anything. I don't really sit around feeling guilty or thinking I'm not good enough. It's just a tough situation, you know? But I don't blame myself for it.

Do you find yourself worrying a lot specifically about the situation at home, like constantly thinking about how to handle things with your father-in-law, even when you're not directly dealing with it?

No, I wouldn't say I'm constantly worrying about it. It's frustrating when I'm there and dealing with him directly, but when I'm at work or out of the house, I'm not really dwelling on it. I just deal with it when it's right in front of me.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like headaches, stomach issues, or muscle tension, that seem to be related to the stress you're feeling at home?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. No stomach issues or headaches. I mean, my back or shoulders might get a little tight sometimes, but... well, I'm an EMT, so that's pretty normal just from lifting patients at work. I wouldn't say I've had any physical problems that I'd connect to the stress at home, no.
When exactly did your father-in-law move in with you?

He moved in about four months ago. It didn't take long for things to get difficult... I'd say I really started noticing the strain within the first couple of months, just as all the new routines and the extra demands of helping out with him started to settle in.
Have you experienced any other major stressors or life changes in the past year, outside of your father-in-law moving in?
No, not really. It's just been the usual stuff at work, but nothing major. The only big change has been him moving in. Everything else has stayed pretty much the same.
Do you think your irritability and stress started specifically because of the change in living situation with your father-in-law, or have you noticed similar feelings even before he moved in?

It definitely started specifically because of him moving in. I didn't have these kinds of feelings before. I mean, my job can be stressful, obviously, but I was handling things just fine. This kind of constant edge I'm on... that really only started after the house got crowded and our routine got turned upside down. So yeah, I'd definitely tie it to the living situation.
